analysis.title: Asia Open - Calendar chaos
key_insights: A more dovish-than-expected Fed outcome pushed UST yields lower and weighed on the dollar, with DXY down 0.30% to 101.88 after Wednesday's Fed hold.
The ECB held rates, and a marginally hawkish Lagarde kept December tightening expectations intact. Citi says if inflation continues to firm, a December hike remains in play.
Headline US equity indices fell, led by Alphabet (-13%) after a miss in search growth (+12%). Breadth stayed strong, with SPX equal-weight up about 1.2%.
Eli Lilly (+7%) and Merck (+4%) rose after results, offsetting some of the tech weakness.
Amazon fell after earnings because AWS growth of +39% was short of expectations. Intel fell over 20% on guidance of $15-$16bn that was well below consensus.
Spot VIX was contained and VVIX fell from 110 last week, but skew remains steep.
EURUSD dropped as much as 0.4% to 1.1105 after the ECB hold, a 17-month low, then pared losses quickly.

The BoJ is expected to hold, with 20bps priced for a December hike. Citi's trader says a perceived dovish BoJ outcome has several times sparked a yen rally that was followed by official action. Citi's base case is a 25bp BoJ hike in December.

USTs extended gains on equity weakness and a more dovish press conference from Fed Chair Warsh. The 2y yield is near 4.60%, down nearly 10bps, and the 5s30s spread widened to about 55bps from about 50bps.
US Q3 GDP rose 3.4% QoQ, driven by AI-related investment and partly offset by surging imports. Core PCE rose 0.32% MoM versus Citi's economist forecast of 0.31%.
The $44 billion 7-year note auction stopped at 4.845% with a bid/cover of 2.33, at the 36th percentile of the past 12 auctions.

Brent rose to $116. Iran said its positions on ending the war will not be compromised after a letter from US VP Vance. Shell CEO Wael Sawan said the high oil price no longer looks like a temporary spike because global inventories are depleted.
US natural gas futures fell late in the session after a storage report showed inventories rising more than expected.

MXN was the weakest LatAm currency. Citi's trader holds a core long USDMXN position into Friday's GDP and next week's rate decision, with pressure for a Banxico cut building. USDMXN topped out at 18.89.
On the eFX desk, volumes were well above average after the ECB. Net flows skewed to NOK and SEK, leveraged accounts bought JPY and MXN, and outflows tilted to CHF and DKK.
In Europe, the rates desk saw hedge funds buying 30y OATs versus 10y and selling 15y versus 20y OATs.
